defaults.permitted_development: A rear extension can be permitted development in Wales if it stays within the Class A rear limits. Single-storey and more-than-one-storey rear extensions follow different depth tests.

rules.height_rules: A single-storey rear extension should not exceed 4m in height. Eaves should not be higher than the eaves of the existing part of the house they project from, and no rear extension should exceed the existing roof height.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor.
rules.boundary_rules: Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m and overall height there should not exceed 4m. Upper floors to a rear extension must be at least 10.5m from the rear boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Verandas, raised platforms, roof terraces and projecting balconies are not part of this permitted development route.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor.
rules.boundary_rules: Where any part is within 2m of a boundary, eaves should not exceed 3m and overall height there should not exceed 4m. Upper floors to a rear extension must be at least 10.5m from the rear boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Verandas, raised platforms, roof terraces and projecting balconies are not part of this permitted development route.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls in Wales narrow these rights. Side extensions on designated land are more restricted, two-storey side extensions are not permitted there, and Article 4 directions can remove further rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually needed for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be required.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales a rear extension may stay within permitted development, but only where it satisfies the Class A depth, height and boundary controls for either a single-storey or more-than-one-storey scheme.

rules.height_rules: Keep single-storey rear work within 4m overall height and do not lift the eaves above the part of the house it projects from. No rear extension should exceed the existing roof height.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary distance matters twice in Wales: near-boundary parts should keep within the 3m eaves and 4m height limits, and any upper floor to a rear extension should stay at least 10.5m from the rear boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Keep the roof form quiet and subordinate. Prominent front-facing changes, roof terraces and bulky additions are more likely to need express permission in the National Park.
rules.materials_rules: Match the new wall and roof finishes closely to the existing house so the rear addition reads as part of the dwelling rather than a separate block.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are tighter in Bannau Brycheiniog National Park. Side and prominent extensions should be checked through the authority before relying on householder rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on householder permitted development for a listed building. Bannau Brycheiniog expects listed building proposals to be properly evidenced, and listed building consent will usually be required.

rules.permitted_development: The Welsh rear-extension route depends on which form is proposed. Single-storey and more-than-one-storey rear extensions have different depth limits, but both still need to stay within the Class A height and boundary rules.

rules.height_rules: Welsh rear-extension height control is straightforward: single-storey work stays within 4m, eaves do not rise above the host eaves, and no rear addition should overtop the existing roof.
rules.depth_rules: A single-storey rear extension can project up to 4m beyond the original rear wall. A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor.
rules.boundary_rules: Rear extensions that run close to the boundary need careful height control. Keep near-boundary parts within 3m eaves and 4m overall height, and keep upper floors 10.5m from the back boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Keep roof design subordinate and avoid assuming that a roof change attached to the extension is permitted. Prominent roof alterations should be checked through pre-application advice.
rules.materials_rules: Use wall and roof materials that closely relate to the existing house. Obvious mismatches can make a rear extension look heavier than it needs to.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are strong in Eryri. Extensions in conservation areas, and prominent side or front-related work elsewhere in the Park, should be checked formally.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent is required for works affecting the character of a listed building in Eryri, and planning permission may also be needed.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls are tighter in Pembrokeshire Coast National Park. Side elements, prominent extensions and conservation area sites should be checked formally before work starts.
